title: Lock Replacement & Door Handle Repair in Sanur Villas
meta: Stuck lock or wobbly handle? Find out how salt air and sand wear down villa door hardware, when to replace it, and simple fixes you can try first.
intro: If your villa door lock has started sticking, your handle feels loose, or fine sand keeps working its way into the mechanism, you are not alone. Sanur's coastal air accelerates corrosion on metal hardware far faster than inland conditions would. This guide walks through what to check, when a small fix will do, and when a full replacement is the smarter move.

paragraphs: Sanur sits right on the water, so every piece of exposed metal on your villa breathes salty, humid air day after day. Add the fine volcanic dust that blows off the road and you get a slow but steady build-up inside locks, hinges, and handle mechanisms. Most expats notice the problem only when the key starts grinding or the handle drops slightly when pressed.

A quick monthly check saves a lot of hassle later. Wipe the outside of the lock cylinder with a dry cloth, look for orange-brown streaks around the keyhole, and gently work the handle up and down. If you feel grit or hear a faint crunch, the internal pins are already corroding.
bullets: Wipe the keyhole and surrounding plate with a dry microfiber cloth once a month.
Lubricate the cylinder with a dry PTFE spray (not oil-based WD-40, which attracts more sand).
Tighten any loose screws on the handle rose while you are there.
If rust has eaten through the surface, do not keep forcing the key; call for an assessment.

paragraphs: A stuck lock is not always a dead one. Before ordering a new unit, try these steps: remove the key, tap the base of the door lightly to dislodge trapped sand, apply a small amount of graphite powder into the keyway, and work the key in and out ten times slowly. For a wobbly handle, open the two small screws on the faceplate, re-seat the spindle, and tighten evenly.

If the mechanism still binds after that, or if the cylinder shows visible pitting and flaking metal, replacement is the right call. Take clear photos of the existing lock from three angles – front, side, and the back plate inside the door – along with a photo of the key itself. Send them over and the technician can identify the type, size, and whether a matching part is available locally before anyone drives across Sanur.

Pricing depends entirely on the job: a simple cylinder swap is different from replacing a full mortise assembly on an old villa gate. The quote comes after reviewing your photos, so there are no surprises at the door.

sections.h2: Common Lock Types in Sanur Villas
paragraphs: Older Balinese-style villas often use a basic pin-tumbler cylinder behind a brass or zinc escutcheon. Newer builds near Jalan Raya Manggis tend to have European-profile mortise locks with a separate deadbolt bolt. Garden gates frequently carry a large padlock or a sliding bolt with a small hasp lock.

The good news is that most of these types are stocked by hardware shops in Sanur and Legian, so you rarely need to wait for a special order. The tricky part is matching the back-plate length and the spindle diameter; two millimetres off and the handle will not sit flush. That is why sending a clear side photo of the existing mechanism saves a second visit.
bullets: Pin-tumbler cylinder (most common on front doors).
Mortise lock with strike plate (newer villas, double doors).
Sliding-bolt latch with a small key lock (service entrances).

paragraphs: A well-maintained lock is only as strong as its neighbours. Check that your gate latch still engages fully – sand can wedge it open just enough for a determined hand. Make sure window handles on the ground floor close tightly; a loose sash lock gives away more access than most owners realise.

Do not mix different brands of lubricant in the same cylinder, and avoid using cooking oil or butter as a quick fix; they gum up inside the pins within a week. If you smell gas near an outdoor kitchen or hear a strange electrical buzz from a doorbell transformer while working around water features, stop what you are doing and call a qualified professional before touching anything further.

sections.h2: Keys: Lost, Broken, or Needing Copies
paragraphs: Losing a villa key in Sanur is stressful but manageable. If the key broke off inside the cylinder, do not keep pushing new keys in; you will push the fragment deeper. A technician can extract the piece with a small hook tool in minutes.

For routine copies, several key-cutting shops along Jalan Sanur and in the Legian area handle standard European and American profiles. For less common Balinese-style keys or high-security cylinders, the shop may need to order a blank, so allow a day or two. If you have had a break-in or suspect someone copied your key without permission, re-keying the cylinder (swapping the internal pin set) is usually faster and cheaper than replacing the whole lock.

faq.q: My lock sticks only when it rains. Is that normal?
faq.a: A little stiffness after heavy rain is common in Sanur because moisture seeps into the cylinder. Wipe it dry, apply graphite powder, and work the key a few times. If the sticking persists for more than a week or you see rust flaking, book an inspection before the pins seize completely.

faq.q: Can I just buy any replacement cylinder from a hardware shop?
faq.a: Not always. The back-plate length, spindle diameter, and key profile all have to match your door's existing mortise. Send photos of the current lock and key first; the technician will confirm whether a standard off-the-shelf part fits or if a specific size is needed.

faq.q: How often should I service my villa locks?
faq.a: In Sanur's coastal conditions, a quick wipe-down and PTFE lubrication every month keeps things running smoothly. A full check – tightening screws, inspecting for corrosion, testing latch engagement – makes sense at least twice a year, ideally before the rainy season hits.
